questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place with a lot of culture and fun

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Before arrival we received emails from University of Milan explaining what to do. It was also very easy to reach them via email with questions

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to go to the university a few days after arrival for the "proof of attendance", and I could just ask any questions I had

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Just send the university an email if you have any doubts, they are always very helpful

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy but also a bit expensive

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Make sure that you live in a safe and fun part of the city! Even though it might be a bit more expensive, living in a nice neighbourhood close to good restaurants, bars and culture is worth it. I lived near Porta Venezia which I can recommend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You receive an email from the university that explains the process and it was very easy

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You receive an email with a link to which courses you can take. Then you just fill out a form with the info for the courses that you want. I got all the courses I wanted and my experience is that everyone did. I changed some of the courses after arrival which was also very easy. There wasn't really a deadline to change courses so you can try out different ones and then just change your course registration at UNIMi after a week or two.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I just sent an email to Massimo with my questions and he answered very fast

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about course registration. Just follow the steps in the mails from UNIMI and ask Massimo questions if you have any.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Much easier courses than at UCPH which was nice. I did not have to study at home a lot, but attendance was mandatory for a lot of courses so I still learned many new things

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is mostly just the professor talking. In some of the courses, we had to do class presentations but that was fine and we could do it in groups. People did not participate much in the classes I had, only a few people.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Comparative Labour Law, 2) International Refugee protection and sustainable development, 3) Law and policies of social rights protection in Europe, 4) European monetary and economic law and 5) International, European and comparative environmental law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Comparative Labour Law was interesting and a good introduction to labour law. It focused on very relevant areas of labour law such as platform workers. Super nice and fun professor. The exam was either an oral exam or a written exam with 20 multiple choice questions and two open questions. I took the written exam which was easy, but take the oral exam!! It was even more chill, students were just asked a couple of basic questions.
European monetary and economic law was interesting and had an oral exam where you presented about a topic you choose yourself. 
Law and policies was very easy and the professor was nice. The exam was a written paper on a topic that you choose yourself and there was a short oral exam where you just explained parts of your written paper to your professor (kind of like a synopsis eksamen).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not join any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ECN arranged events that were alright in the beginning to meet people

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to some of the ECN events in the beginning to meet other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Going to football games at San Siro! Lake Como and Bergamo are very nice and easy to get to from Milan. I also took the train to Venice, Rome and Firence which was fun!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. They are more relaxed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just ask if they want to grab a coffee or an aperol after class

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That teachers and students were sometimes very late

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the bars, the football matches at San Siro. People are very nice, fun and chatty

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don't be afraid to ask people if they want to go out to dinner, bars or anything. I went on exchange on my own and found out that everyone was eager to get to know each other and have fun so just be open and reach reach out to people
2) Time goes by very fast so enjoy it
3) Do fun things such as travel in the weekends and be spontaneous

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seats in some classrooms are limited so be early to class if you want a good seat

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing people from home. BUT don't have too many visits from home, because you also want to spend weekends and free time with your new friends

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
